data.content_ref: inline:The target's central claim asserts resilience 'if and only if' a graph-entropy metric exceeds an undefined 'internal diversity coefficient,' yet it never supplies the evidence criterion the problem explicitly demands: how to distinguish truly independent failures from failures merely appearing uncorrelated until a shared cause is found. Its own countercondition (shared K8s/cloud stack) is a textbook hidden-correlation case, but the target fails to state what evidence would expose that hidden correlation pre-failure — e.g., measured propagation of incidents across operators sharing the same upstream image, time-series co-failures under load, or dependency-graph audit of shared managed substrates. Without such an evidence-specification, the biconditional is unfalsifiable: any observed lack of correlation can be re-explained post-hoc by invoking an unmeasured shared trigger, which is exactly the epistemic trap the question asks the answer to disarm.
